title: cap-table coverage_disclosure.json
$comment: CLOSED 2026-08-31 at EVERY object level -- top level, `reconciliation` AND `metadata`. The first pass closed the first two and left `metadata` open, which reinstated the exact hole one level down: a richer payload nested under `metadata` validated clean. If you add a nested object here, close it in the same edit. The 2026-07-05 incident's failure mode was an ad-hoc RICHER payload -- extra keys, not missing ones -- so a validator that only checks `required` accepts it unchanged. Top-level `additionalProperties: false` alone does not close a nested `{"type": "object"}` with no `properties`, which is what `reconciliation` was: a richer payload nests inside it and validates clean. This is a deliberate, narrow exception to the standing decision not to add `additionalProperties: false` generically -- the general objection is that it rejects valid inputs, which does not apply to a fixed disclosure form whose whole purpose is to be a fixed disclosure form. Do NOT generalize it to the other cap-table schemas. ENFORCEMENT IS PARTIAL, and the closure describes the document rather than every writer: `_cap_table_schema_validator.py` silently IGNORES `additionalProperties` (its own docstring says so), so `compose_report.py` and `compose_extraction_report.py` -- both writing via `_artifact_writer.write_artifact` -- do not enforce it. Only `write_coverage_disclosure.py`'s validator does. That is the hand-roll route, which is the route the 2026-07-05 incident took, so the closure covers the case it was written for -- but do not read it as a fleet-wide guarantee.
